references.title: (Illustrative) Synth macro: 'every button, one take'
references.why: Product truth as spectacle: extreme macro of real materials with diegetic clicks made the object feel expensive. Transferable: sound-led macro cut on each physical action. Figures illustrative (a real entry cites the post page).

scenes: 0-1s: hook, finger presses a key in extreme macro, loud click
1-8s: eight 1s macro cuts, each on a new control, each with its own sound
8-12s: pull back to reveal the whole device on a desk
structure.pacing: 1s cuts locked to the device's own sounds, one 4s hold on the reveal
structure.music: None: diegetic sound only, building into a beat made from the clicks
structure.hook: An unexpectedly loud, satisfying physical click in the first frame

references.title: (Illustrative) Creator POV: 'day 1 vs day 100 of running at 6am'
references.why: A transformation format with a built-in payoff; the product (shoes) is the constant across both halves. Transferable: split structure with a hard match cut. Figures illustrative.

scenes: 5-6s: match cut on the shoe hitting the ground
structure.pacing: Slow, messy first half; match cut; fast, clean second half
structure.music: Trending audio with a beat drop placed exactly on the match cut
structure.hook: Relatable text overlay plus a sound everyone knows (alarm)

references.title: (Illustrative) Kinetic type launch: 'three words, three seconds each'
references.why: Bold typography carries the message while footage stays secondary, so it reads with sound off. Transferable: oversized type cut-outs revealing footage through the letters. Comments and shares not public (null).

scenes: 0-1s: one giant word fills the frame
1-7s: footage revealed through letterforms, word changes every 2s
structure.pacing: Hard cuts every 2s, type animates on the beat
structure.hook: A single oversized word that the viewer reads before they can scroll

references.title: (Illustrative) Deadpan mockumentary: 'the office that banned meetings'
references.why: Comedy sells a workflow product without a feature list; very high share ratio. Transferable: one absurd premise, a talking head, and the product as the punchline. Figures illustrative.

scenes: 0-2s: talking head, deadpan line that states the absurd premise
2-14s: three quick cutaways proving the premise
14-20s: product UI on a laptop is the reveal and punchline
structure.pacing: Talking head holds, cutaways snap; the comedic pause is kept
structure.hook: A deadpan first line that makes no sense yet

takeaways: Lead with a physical or audible action in frame 1, not a logo (ref-1, ref-2)
Build the structure around one cut that pays off: a match cut or a reveal (ref-2, ref-4)
Let type carry the message so it works with sound off (ref-3)
Use the product's own sounds or a straight-faced score rather than generic hype music (ref-1, ref-4)
diversityNote: Four formats (macro product, creator POV, kinetic type, mockumentary), four platforms of origin, three music approaches. Excluded the obvious picks: the brand's own most famous hero ad and any 'cinematic slow-motion athlete' montage, because every competitor copies them.
